text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The introduction of a currency board is the only way to lead Bulgaria out of the current crisis, said opposition Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov, wrapping up a visit to Washington where he consulted with International Monetary Fund officials. He said the opposition would seek a national consensus for early parliamentary elections and a new central bank board.
-- From December 10, Bulgarian airport fees will be collected in dollars, said the chief of the air controllers department at Sofia Airport, Valentin Valkov.

-- The finance ministry should pay over 15 billion levs and $4.3 million in the first half of December as interest on government securities issued to guarantee deposits in the first five commercial banks put in receivership by the central bank earlier this year.
-- Bulgaria's cumulative inflation for 1996 is expected to reach 260 percent by the year-end, finance ministry experts said.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank should sell some 300 million dollars from its reserves to curb the lev slump on the local forex market and avoid hyperinflation, a member of the BNB plenary council, Georgi Petrov, told the national radio.

-- Belgian consortium Solvay submitted a revised offer for a 60 percent stake in Bulgaria's Sodi Devnya chemical plant, raising their bid to $160 million from $112 million to match the leading bid from U.S. General Chemical Inc, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's main economic problems are rising inflation, sharp lev depreciation, destabilisation in the banking system and falling central bank reserves, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said in a report on the cabinet's performance.

-- The International Monetary Fund has demanded the introduction of a currency board in Bulgaria from January 1 with the lev pegged to the German mark, said Krassimir Angarski, who will be appointed economic adviser to president elect Petar Stoyanov and who took part in talks with the IMF in Washington.
